exposure: congenital malformations, deformations, and chromosomal abnormalities
cohort: The study included 186,583 live births in Miyazaki Prefecture, Japan, between 2003 and 2022.
finding: Congenital malformations, deformations, and chromosomal abnormalities were the most common cause of early neonatal death (48.6%), followed by complications of intrapartum events (12.4%), infection (9.5%), and low birth weight and prematurity (9.5%), with Trisomy 18 being the most common specific cause, and trends in incidence remained unchanged over the 20-year period.
